You can learn how to pronounce new words more easily if you know some simple rules about suffixes and word stress.

You can learn how to stress a word by paying attention to the rules for certain suffixes. A suffix is the ending of a word that adds meaning to that word. Knowing the meaning of suffixes can help you to build your vocabulary and allow you to express yourself in different ways using different words.
Let's look at the following suffixes and their pronunciation rules for word stress.

images.text:
Hear ye! Hear ye! Friends, Romans, Countrymen! Lend me your ears! My name is Paula Timbers and I am so happy to be here giving my first Toastmasters address. I would like to give a special thanks to my friend Howard Taylor who signed my petition to join the club.
Today I would like to talk to you about my recent trip to China. I went with three other brave employees from my office. I am convinced that going on this trip was a great decision. In preparation for the trip, I read several histories of China and also learned about Chinese language and philosophy. In my opinion, the best language course I found was the classic series called Getting By in Chinese. I also read through several travel guidebooks to be able to identify some major landmarks.

When I arrived in Beijing, I found that the legacy of Chairman Mao is prominent everywhere.  I walked around for nearly an hour and a half, soaking up the ambiance of the busy streets, buildings and traffic. As a Canadian traffic engineer, I was fascinated to see horses, pedicabs and cars parked on sidewalks, and all manner of transport on the side streets. You have to be adaptable to get around in China.

Tienanmen Square is the largest public square in the world — the size of 90 football fields.  It was filled with soccer players, kite-flyers and lots and lots of people who were just walking about. I stopped to chat with a couple who told me they were students. I suspect they wanted to practice their English.  They said they were students of art and calligraphy, and invited me to look at their work. What an experience!
